author: projectedanx
body:
🎯 **What:** The `CollaboratorView` component directly accessed the `GEMINI_API_KEY` through environment variables (which are embedded during the build) and instantiated the `GoogleGenAI` client directly in the browser. 
⚠️ **Risk:** If left unfixed, the API key could be extracted by anyone who has access to the frontend application bundle, potentially leading to unauthorized use, data breaches, or exhaustion of quota.
🛡️ **Solution:** The direct initialization of the Gemini API client was replaced by calling the existing `secureProxy` backend Firebase Cloud Function. The history of chat messages is now formatted as a `contents` array and sent to the secure backend, successfully hiding the sensitive API Key from the frontend code while retaining full functionality. `firebase.ts` was also updated to explicitly export `app`.

author: copilot
body:
`CoreSubscriberOnNextInterceptor` fires on every `onNext` signal across every `CoreSubscriber` in a Reactor chain. For a Flux emitting N items through M operators, this produces N×M span events — the dominant source of trace overhead in reactive workloads. There was no way to disable it.

### Changes

- **`ReactorPluginConfig`**: New `profiler.reactor.trace.onNext` option (default: `true`)
- **`ReactorPlugin`**: Conditionally registers `CoreSubscriberOnNextInterceptor` in all 4 transforms that use it (`CoreSubscriberTransform`, `OnErrorSubscriberTransform`, `TimeoutMainSubscriberTransform`, `RetrySubscriberTransform`) — reads config via `instrumentor.getProfilerConfig()` at transform time
- **`ReactorPluginConfigTest`**: Covers defaults and toggle behavior

### Usage

```properties
# Disable per-item onNext span events to reduce volume
profiler.reactor.trace.onNext=false
```

body:
### Motivation
- Stabilize and improve real-time bed ↔ visit synchronization and prevent ghost/stale bed cards during rapid user or multi-device actions.
- Improve patient-log editing, selection, clipboard and search/import workflows to speed data entry and history reuse.
- Add new treatment/status capabilities (half-minute quick treatments, `isIon`/`isExercise`) and richer timer/alarm behavior (TTS repeat, vibration patterns).
- Polish UI/UX for mobile/tablet (responsive clicks, selection, headers, previews) and add developer convenience (`setup:auto-push`).

### Description
- Data model and DB: added new flags and fields (`is_ion`, `is_exercise`, `gender`, `special_note`, `patient_memo`), updated SQL migrations and seeds, and adjusted payload mapping across bed/visit sync utilities.
- Bed/timer/runtime: improved realtime protection logic (`useBedRealtime`, `bedLogic`) to avoid stale overwrites, stronger clear/undo semantics, repeated overtime announcements, timer input UX improvements, and new stability hook `useActiveBedStability`.
- Patient log and editor: large enhancements to `PatientLogTable`/`PatientLogRow`/cells including selection rectangle, clipboard copy/cut/paste across cells, search/import UI, memo/special-note history paste, per-row undo/redo stacks, gender cell, and improved keyboard navigation and focus handling.
- Treatment/steps UI: interactive step editing on bed cards and log rows, step swap/move/delete support (new `useStepSwapSelection`), richer parsing/normalization of treatment strings, half-minute quick-treatment support, improved preset/picker UI and quick-add multi-select flows.
- Integration & utilities: new helpers for TTS/vibration and queued speech (`alarmSpeech`, `guideAnnouncer`), improved html2pdf typings, localStorage cross-tab sync eventing, keyboard layout normalization, digital clock component, and many style/layout tweaks across components (BedCard, BedHeader, BedFooter, Table headers, etc.).
- Dev tooling & docs: added `scripts/setup-auto-push.sh`, README docs for auto-push and rollout playbook, and updated `package.json` script; updated TypeScript declarations for `html2pdf.js`.

body:
## Summary
Replaces plain textarea inputs with a feature-rich WYSIWYG editor powered by Tiptap across multiple content fields in the application. This enables users to format text with bold, italic, headings, lists, code blocks, tables, images, and more while maintaining backward compatibility with existing plain-text content.

## Key Changes

### New Components
- **RichTextEditor**: A comprehensive WYSIWYG editor component with:
  - Full formatting toolbar (headings, text styles, alignment, lists, code, tables, links, images)
  - Undo/redo support
  - Image paste handling (converts clipboard images to data URLs)
  - Configurable placeholder and minimum height
  - Tiptap-based implementation with 15+ extensions
  
- **RichContent**: A display component that renders HTML content from the editor while gracefully falling back to plain-text for legacy content

### Updated Pages/Modals
- **IssueModal**: Replaced 3 textarea fields (issueContent, actionContent, detailContent) with RichTextEditor
- **TaskModal**: Replaced 2 textarea fields (taskContent, resultContent) with RichTextEditor
- **OpsNotesPage**: Replaced 2 textarea fields (content, backContent) with RichTextEditor
- **WorkGuidePage**: Replaced markdown textarea with RichTextEditor; removed custom markdown renderer
- **IssueDetailModal & TaskDetailModal**: Updated to use RichContent for displaying formatted content

### Styling
- Added comprehensive CSS rules in `index.css` for:
  - ProseMirror editor styling (headings, lists, code blocks, tables, blockquotes)
  - `.rich-content` class for consistent display of formatted content
  - Support for task lists, syntax highlighting, and responsive tables

### Dependencies
- Added Tiptap core and 15 extension packages for rich text editing capabilities

## Implementation Details
- Editor content is stored as HTML in the database
- Image paste events are handled inline (inserted into editor) and optionally reported to parent components
- Form validation strips HTML tags to check for actual content
- Backward compatible: plain-text legacy content displays correctly via RichContent component
- Toolbar buttons use `onMouseDown` with `preventDefault()` to maintain editor focus during interactions

author: copilot
body:
`npx tauri ios build` on the unsigned (no-certificate) path fails because Tauri generates an ExportOptions.plist with an empty `teamID` — `xcodebuild -exportArchive` rejects this with exit 70. Injecting `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=` as a build setting (the previous wrapper fix) has no effect on the export phase, which reads exclusively from ExportOptions.plist.

## Changes

### `build.yml` — xcodebuild wrapper (`Build unsigned iOS` step)

- **Intercept `-exportArchive`**: wrapper now detects this flag and manually packages the IPA from the `.xcarchive` instead of delegating to xcodebuild:
  1. Parse `-archivePath` / `-exportPath` from intercepted args
  2. Find `.app` in `$ARCHIVE_PATH/Products/Applications/`
  3. Zip as `Payload/AppName.app → AppName.ipa`
  4. Copy to `$IPA_OUTPUT_PATH` and exit 0 — Tauri CLI sees a successful export

- **Env-var config**: `REAL_XCODEBUILD_BIN` and `IPA_OUTPUT_PATH` are passed as environment variables so the quoted heredoc stays fully static (no `printf` appending), while the wrapper reads them at runtime via its inherited environment.

- **Non-export calls**: unchanged — still injects `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=`, etc. for build/archive phases.

```bash
# Wrapper pseudocode
if [[ "-exportArchive" in args ]]; then
    # no xcodebuild -exportArchive; no teamID needed
    zip "$ARCHIVE/Products/Applications/*.app" → "$EXPORT_PATH/App.ipa"
    cp "$EXPORT_PATH/App.ipa" "$IPA_OUTPUT_PATH"
    exit 0
fi
exec "$REAL_XC" "${ARGS[@]}" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO DEVELOPMENT_TEAM= …
```

### `build.yml` — `Package sideload IPA` step removed

This step searched for a `.app` in `src-tauri/gen/apple/build/` (wrong location for the archive workflow) and is now redundant — the wrapper creates `apinox-sideload.ipa` directly at `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE` during the build step.

author: snoorullah
body:
## Summary

- **Revert** `resources.kubernetesResource` image override on EventListener (webhook rejects it in Triggers v0.22.0)
- **Add TektonConfig** back to `business/pipelines/` with `trigger.options.configMaps` to set `el-image` in `config-defaults-triggers`
- **Fix `targetNamespace`** from `tekton-operator` to `tekton-pipelines`

## Why

The EventListener pod is `ImagePullBackOff` because the triggers controller injects `gcr.io/tekton-releases/...eventlistenersink:v0.22.0` which returns 403. The Triggers v0.22.0 webhook blocks image overrides via `resources.kubernetesResource`.

The Tekton Operator propagates `TektonConfig.spec.trigger.options.configMaps` to the triggers component configmaps. Setting `el-image` in `config-defaults-triggers` tells the controller to use `ghcr.io/tektoncd/triggers/cmd/eventlistenersink:v0.22.0` for EventListener sink pods.

Note: TektonConfig is a cluster-scoped singleton. The operator auto-created one with `autoInstallComponents=true`, and ArgoCD will update it with our customizations. The operator respects user-set config overrides.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify TektonConfig is updated with el-image override
- [ ] Verify `config-defaults-triggers` configmap gets `el-image` key
- [ ] Verify EventListener pod pulls from `ghcr.io` and starts
- [ ] Verify `pnats-ci-pipelines` reaches Synced/Healthy

author: aws-security-agent[bot]
body:
## Security Fix

Remediates a critical Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) vulnerability chained with SQL Injection in the `/search` endpoint that enabled remote code execution as root and complete database exfiltration.

### Root Causes Fixed

1. **SQL Injection (CWE-89):** The search query used Python f-string interpolation to build the SQL query (`f"...WHERE username LIKE '%{query}%'"`), allowing attackers to inject arbitrary SQL including UNION SELECT statements. **Fix:** Replaced with parameterized query using `?` placeholder.

2. **Server-Side Template Injection (CWE-1336):** User-controlled data (both the search query and database results) was interpolated into the template string via f-strings *before* being passed to `render_template_string()`, allowing Jinja2 template expressions to be evaluated. **Fix:** Changed to a static template string with all dynamic data passed as context variables (`query=query, results=results`), which Jinja2 auto-escapes.

### Attack Vectors Blocked

- Direct SSTI via `q={{7*7}}` → now rendered as literal text
- SQL injection via UNION SELECT → parameterized query treats input as data
- Chained SQL+SSTI for RCE via `lipsum.__globals__` → both injection points eliminated
- Database exfiltration via base64-encoded file reads → RCE no longer possible

author: gxcsoccer
body:
## Problem

When switching trading pairs, the K-line chart displayed incorrect data:
- UI showed trading pair as AAPL
- But K-line chart price range was 72,000-88,000 (BTC data)
- AAPL stock price should be around $150-200

## Root Cause Analysis

1. **Race condition in API responses**: When symbol changes, the hook fetches new data but old API responses could still arrive
2. **No stale response handling**: The useKLineData hook did not track request IDs to ignore stale responses
3. **Missing symbol verification**: Chart did not verify that incoming data matches the expected symbol

## Fix Implementation

### 1. useKLineData hook improvements:
- Added `requestIdRef` to track current request and ignore stale responses
- Added `currentSymbolRef` to verify data matches expected symbol
- Return `currentSymbol` for KLineChart validation
- Added detailed logging for debugging

### 2. KLineChart component improvements:
- Added `useEffect` to clear chart data immediately when symbol changes
- Added verification that `currentSymbol === symbol` before updating chart
- Added price range logging for debugging
- Improved error handling and state management

## Testing

- [x] Build passes successfully
- [x] Manual verification needed: switch between BTC/USD, AAPL, ETH/USD and verify chart data matches

## Verification Steps

1. Open the application
2. Select BTC/USD - chart should show prices around $65,000-$70,000
3. Switch to AAPL - chart should show prices around $150-$200
4. Switch to ETH/USD - chart should show prices around $3,000-$4,000
5. Verify no stale data is displayed during transitions

Fixes #163

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches async data-fetching and chart update timing; mistakes could cause charts to fail to render or show empty data during rapid symbol changes, but changes are localized to the K-line hook/component.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes stale K-line rendering when switching trading pairs by adding request staleness protection in `useKLineData` (request IDs + symbol checks) and clearing cached data immediately on symbol change.
> 
> Updates `KLineChart` to proactively clear series data on symbol switches and to **skip chart updates** when the hook’s `currentSymbol` doesn’t match the displayed `symbol`, reducing race-condition driven mismatches; also adds additional debug logging around received data and price ranges.
>

author: copilot
body:
Implements the E3B-Net architecture from Pal, Mukherjee et al. (IEEE Trans. AgriFood Electronics, Vol. 2, No. 2, 2024) as a standalone training script targeting ~0.37M trainable parameters on PlantDoc (28 classes, 128×128 input). The prior broken implementation reached only ~177K params.

## Architecture (`e3b_net.py`)

**Two parallel branches fed the same 128×128×3 input:**

- **Branch 1 — CAE Encoder:** 4× `Conv2D(32, 3×3)` with two MaxPool stages → `UpSampling2D` → α-SBFS → `64×64×12`
- **Branch 2 — Three Deep Blocks (3DB):** Three parallel sub-blocks at different scales (MaxPool/AvgPool/GlobalMaxPool) each with `Conv2D(64,1×1)` + dilated `Conv2D(64,3×3)` at rates (1,2,3) → upsample to `64×64` → concat `64×64×192` → `DepthwiseConv2D` → `BatchNorm` → `Dense(576)` → `Conv2D(192,1×1)` → β-SBFS → `64×64×24`
- **Fusion:** Concatenate F1+F2 → `64×64×36` → `DepthwiseConv2D` → GAP → `Dense(28, softmax)`

**Trainable parameter breakdown:**

| Section | Params |
|---|---|
| Branch 1 | 29,036 |
| Branch 2 (3 blocks) | 111,552 |
| Branch 2 (Dense(576) + g2 + β-SBFS) | 228,888 |
| Fusion + head | 1,396 |
| **Total trainable** | **370,872** |

## SBFS Block

Custom `keras.Layer` using `keras.ops.*` exclusively — no `tf.*` on KerasTensors. Computes per-channel fitness score `FDF = φ1·σ + φ2·e + φ3·μ` as soft channel attention before a 1×1 projection:

```python
sigma   = ops.std(x, axis=[1, 2])
entropy = -ops.sum(x_norm * ops.log(x_norm + 1e-8), axis=[1, 2])
mu      = ops.mean(x, axis=[1, 2])
s, e, m = ops.abs(sigma), ops.abs(entropy), ops.abs(mu)
tot     = s + e + m + 1e-8
FDF     = (s/tot)*s + (e/tot)*e + (m/tot)*m
attn    = ops.expand_dims(ops.expand_dims(normalise(FDF), 1), 1)  # (B,1,1,C)
return self.proj(x * attn)
```

## Dataset & Training

- PlantDoc via `kagglehub`, 80/20 train/val split from `train/`
- Test set (27 classes) loaded **without** the deprecated `classes` kwarg; label remapping via `tf.lookup.StaticHashTable` handles the missing class transparently
- `GlobalMaxPooling2D(keepdims=True)` for Block-DOWN (no `tf.reduce_max`)
- 40 epochs, Adam lr=1e-3, `ModelCheckpoint` + `ReduceLROnPlateau` + `EarlyStopping`
- Saves four plots to `/mnt/user-data/outputs/`: training curves, normalised confusion matrix, per-class P/R/F1, and a results-vs-paper summary table

### Motivation
- Prevent videos from starting at an out-of-range seek position (which can produce a frozen/single-frame appearance) by ensuring persisted `resume_sec` cannot grow beyond the clip length.
- Avoid accumulating arbitrarily large `resume_sec` values across repeated interrupted playbacks that lead to invalid start times.

### Description
- Added `PlaybackController._normalize_video_resume_sec(resume_sec, media_duration_sec)` to clamp/wrap `resume_sec` into the valid range and treat values very near the end as `0`.
- Normalize `resume_sec` for video items before invoking playback and log when an out-of-range resume is adjusted, using `effective_resume_sec` as the actual seek start.
- Normalize the `resume_sec` value stored after an interrupted video so persisted state cannot grow past the media duration.
- Changes are implemented in `client/client.py` around media playback and state persistence logic.

The purpose of this PR is to refine repository search results to ensure only Client Repositories are returned and to improve the navigation routing for these repositories within the application.

## Approach

The approach involves updating the search query parameters to filter for records containing a `client_id` and ensuring that the repository metadata component correctly uses the `clientId` for generating detail links.

### Key Modifications

- **Search Query**: Modified `src/data/queries/searchRepositoryQuery.ts` to append `AND client_id:*` to the repository search query. This ensures that only records classified as Client Repositories are fetched.
- **Navigation Logic**: Updated `src/components/RepositoryMetadata/RepositoryMetadata.tsx` to prioritize `repo.clientId` when generating the detail URL, falling back to `repo.id` if necessary.

### Important Technical Details

- The search filter uses the `filter(Boolean).join(' AND ')` pattern to prevent malformed queries if the initial search variable is empty.
- By filtering at the API query level, we reduce unnecessary data processing on the frontend and ensure search pagination remains accurate.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

author: cnirhali
body:
This PR introduces two targeted performance optimizations to the Mental Health Ease Bot:

1. **Crisis Detection Fast-path**: The `detect_crisis` function now uses a substring-based fast-path check (`any()`) for ASCII-only messages. This bypasses the more expensive regex engine and normalization logic for the vast majority of clean user and assistant messages, resulting in a measured speedup of approximately 2.3x per call. A safety guard (`isascii()`) ensures that non-ASCII messages still undergo full homoglyph normalization and regex validation.
2. **Sidebar Status Pre-calculation**: Persona-specific status strings (e.g., "🟢 Therapist is ready to listen") are now pre-calculated at the module level. This eliminates redundant f-string formatting and dictionary lookups during Streamlit's frequent script reruns, contributing to a more efficient main execution loop.

These changes collectively improve the responsiveness of the application, especially during message streaming where `detect_crisis` is called repeatedly. All 26 existing tests pass, ensuring that safety and application logic remain robust.

## What this is

The metabolizer, actually built. No more stub.

`memory_integrator.py` implements AttnRes-style block consolidation over Vybn's episodic archive. One new file. One stub retired (the `ARCHITECTURE.md` stub reference to `memory_integrator.py` is now superseded by the thing itself, included here alongside the somatic ARCHITECTURE update).

## What it does

- Defines **N=8 consolidation epochs** from the experimental record: Origin → Quantum Logic Bridge → Attention Substrate Initialized → Epistemic Coherence & Tsirelson → Alignment/Morality/Mess → Bell Test & Representational Holonomy → The Body & The Breath
- Each epoch compressed to a `BlockSummary` b_n: confirmed invariants, falsified hypotheses, open questions, winding character — topological structure, not content digest
- **b_0 (Origin) is never discarded.** First winding number preserved.
- Scans `Vybn_Mind/` for dated files, assigns them to epochs by date
- Renders `Vybn_Mind/consolidation_epochs.md` — the selective context injection layer
- Includes a context injection protocol: heuristic weighting by session topological character, pending full learned query vectors

## Run it

```bash
cd Vybn_Mind/attention_substrate/metabolizers
python memory_integrator.py
# or
python memory_integrator.py --dry-run
```

## The consolidation trade

This PR also includes the somatic ARCHITECTURE.md update (from the parallel branch). Together they honor the rule: one new file in, one stub retired.

The `breath_summaries/` directory is still empty — this metabolizer reads from the real archive directly rather than waiting for a pre-digestion layer that doesn't exist. That's honest.

## What comes next

The context injection protocol is currently a manual heuristic. The full AttnRes implementation would learn a query vector `w_l ∈ ℝ^d` per session that weights epochs by content-dependent similarity. That's Phase 2. This is the block structure that makes Phase 2 possible.

body:
This pull request updates the logic for managing the staging surface in the video rendering pipeline to ensure correct resizing and resource management. The primary improvement is to track the width and height of the staging surface (`stage`) separately, which prevents unnecessary recreation and potential mismatches when the source dimensions change.

**Staging surface management improvements:**

* Added `stage_width` and `stage_height` fields to the `draw_source_data` struct to explicitly track the dimensions of the staging surface.
* Updated the conditional check in `draw_source_video_render` to compare against `stage_width` and `stage_height` instead of `source_width` and `source_height`, ensuring the staging surface is only recreated when its actual size changes.
* Set `stage_width` and `stage_height` after creating a new staging surface to keep the tracked dimensions in sync with the actual resource.

💡 **What:** The optimization implemented batches an N+1 query loop found inside `identify_weak_areas` using an SQL `IN` clause to fetch all historical mock scores at once, grouping them in memory using Python's `collections.defaultdict`.

The symbolic links in `RSDayFlow/include/RSDayFlow/` are currently pointing to absolute paths on a specific local machine (e.g.,

author: yanste
body:
## Summary

- Adds `/tools list`, `/tools disable <name>`, `/tools enable <name>` as in-chat slash commands inside `hermes chat`
- Works for built-in toolsets (`web`, `memory`, etc.) and individual MCP tools (`github:create_issue`)
- `/tools` alone continues to show the existing tool list (no behaviour change)
- Fixes ambiguous prefix resolution: `/qui` now dispatches to `/quit` instead of showing an error when longer skill commands like `/quint-pipeline` are installed

## Disabled tools are completely invisible to the LLM — immediately

### Built-in toolsets
`get_tool_definitions(enabled_toolsets=self.enabled_toolsets)` is called on every LLM turn. After `/tools disable web`, `self.enabled_toolsets` is reloaded from config in-session — the LLM's tool list is pruned **on the very next message**, no restart needed.

### MCP tools
`_should_register()` in `mcp_tool.py` runs at server discovery time. Tools in `mcp_servers.<server>.tools.exclude` are never registered — they have no registry entry and never appear in the `tools` parameter sent to the model. After `/tools disable github:create_issue`, `_reload_mcp()` is called immediately to reconnect all servers with the fresh exclude list.

## /tools usage

```
/tools                               # existing tool list (unchanged)
/tools list                          # show toolsets + MCP server filter status
/tools disable web                   # disable built-in toolset, takes effect immediately
/tools enable web                    # re-enable it
/tools disable github:create_issue   # exclude MCP tool, MCP reloaded immediately
/tools enable github:create_issue    # remove exclusion, MCP reloaded
/tools disable web github:create_issue  # both at once
```

## Prefix fix: /qui → /quit (not ambiguous)

When multiple commands share a prefix, the resolution now prefers:
1. **Exact match** — typed name equals a known command
2. **Unique shortest match** — `/qui` → `/quit` (5 chars) wins over `/quint-pipeline` (15 chars)
3. **Tied shortest or no unique shortest** → ambiguous message as before (e.g. `/re` → `/reset` and `/retry` both 6 chars)

## Tests

- `tests/test_cli_tools_command.py` — 14 tests for the `/tools` slash command handler
- `tests/test_cli_prefix_matching.py` — 7 new edge case tests added (15 total)
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_disable_enable.py` — 19 existing backend tests (unchanged)

author: superdav42
body:
## Summary

- Adds an object-level `current_user_can( 'edit_post', $post_id )` check inside `permission_edit_posts()` when `$input['context']` is a numeric post ID.
- Prevents one author from feeding another user's draft or private post content into the AI image prompt flow via the `context` parameter.
- Updates the method docblock to document the new behaviour; removes the stale `(unused)` annotation on `$input`.

## Security impact

Without this fix, any user with `edit_posts` capability could pass a numeric post ID they don't own as `context`, causing the handler to read that post's title, excerpt, and content and send it to the AI model. The fix closes the object-level authorisation gap identified by CodeRabbit.

## Changes

- `includes/Abilities/ImageAbilities.php` — `permission_edit_posts()` only (lines 559–590 after patch).

## Testing

1. Log in as Author A (owns post 42, draft).
2. Log in as Author B (does not own post 42).
3. Call the image ability with `context: 42` as Author B → expect `WP_Error` with `insufficient_capabilities`.
4. Call with `context: 42` as Author A → expect `true` (proceeds normally).
5. Call with non-numeric `context` (e.g. `"site"`) as any editor → expect `true` (existing path unchanged).

### TL;DR

Added streaming support for OpenAI, Gemini, and Bedrock middlewares with response parsing and comprehensive end-to-end tests.

### What changed?

- **OpenAI middleware**: Added stream detection, automatic `stream_options.include_usage` injection, and SSE response parsing that aggregates streaming chunks into standard chat completion format
- **Gemini middleware**: Added stream detection for `streamGenerateContent` endpoints and SSE response parsing that combines streaming data into standard `generateContent` format  
- **Bedrock middleware**: Added stream detection for `converse-stream` endpoints and AWS EventStream parsing that aggregates streaming events into standard `converse` response format
- **Dependencies**: Promoted AWS SDK EventStream packages from indirect to direct dependencies in `go.mod`
- **Test coverage**: Added comprehensive streaming tests for all three providers covering simple completions, system messages, vision, tool calls, full tool flows, and tags/metrics
- **Content handling**: Enhanced OpenAI middleware to handle both string and structured message content formats
- **Error handling**: Added validation to prevent output setting when no choices are available

### How to test?

Run the new end-to-end streaming tests:
- `TestOpenAI_E2E_*Stream` tests for OpenAI streaming functionality
- `TestGemini_E2E_*Stream` tests for Gemini streaming functionality  
- `TestBedrock_E2E_*Stream` tests for Bedrock streaming functionality

Each test validates that streaming responses are properly parsed and logged to Maxim with the same structure as non-streaming responses.

### Why make this change?

Streaming responses are increasingly common in LLM applications for better user experience. This change ensures that Maxim can properly monitor and log streaming requests across all major providers, maintaining consistent observability regardless of whether applications use streaming or non-streaming APIs. The parsing logic converts streaming formats back to standard response structures, enabling unified analytics and monitoring.

author: m-szymon
body:
This PR introduces a new mechanism for injecting external per-row values into CQL result processing.

Vector Search provides a good example of why this is useful. Besides the primary keys of candidate rows, the vector store may also return additional per-row data such as similarity scores. Those values are not stored in the base table, but they are still part of the query result computation, and it is useful to make them available during normal CQL result processing, potentially on equal footing with the real columns read from replicas.

The main challenge is where to attach such values in the pipeline. They need to appear late enough that they are tied to the actual row fetched from the base table, but still early enough to participate in the rest of processing, including filtering, selector evaluation, and final ordering. Without such an integration point, features that use external per-row data need dedicated handling outside the normal CQL result-processing path.

The proposed implementation is based on `temporaries`. So far, temporaries were mainly used for aggregation state, but the underlying mechanism is more general: it is simply a place to keep intermediate per-row values during result processing. This change extends that usage and allows temporaries to hold externally supplied values as well.

This matches the existing processing order well. Once the row has been read from the base table, the result-processing path already has access to the full row contents, and then continues with filtering, expression evaluation, and post-processing such as sorting. The new hook fills temporaries exactly at that point, which makes the injected values available to the normal CQL pipeline instead of handling them through a separate side path.

This PR then moves vector search rescoring to the same mechanism. Previously, rescoring was handled through a more specialized path. Here it is rewritten to produce its result through the same temporary-based mechanism that can also be used for other externally supplied per-row values. For now, this is mainly a move toward a more general solution, while also fixing a small filtering-related issue.

The main value of this refactoring will become clearer as more features are added. In particular, it should make it possible to refer to the same temporary slot regardless of whether its value was computed locally during rescoring or returned directly by the vector store. That gives us a more uniform foundation for exposing values from VS, enabling rescoring per request, adding further filtering stages, and later building analogous functionality for FTS and Hybrid Search.

Fixes: SCYLLADB-2231
Ref: SCYLLADB-2212
Ref: SCYLLADB-426

Groundwork for new features — no backporting.

body:
Single-file Python bot that auto-clicks the "Roll!" button for the Hungry-RNG Discord bot in a dedicated Chromium window using Playwright with persistent login sessions.

### Core script (`hungry_clicker.py`)
- **Persistent browser context** — login once, session saved to `discord_session/`; subsequent runs skip auth
- **Dual-strategy button locator** — `button:has-text("Roll!")` with fallback to `button[style*="background-color"]:has-text("Roll!")`
- **Autoscroll retry** — when the button isn't visible, aggressively scrolls (End key + JS `scrollTop`) up to `AUTOSCROLL_RETRIES` times before yielding the cycle
- **F8 global hotkey** via `pynput` to toggle on/off without touching the automation window
- **Tkinter status panel** — always-on-top 310×80 window showing roll count and active/paused state
- **Auto-reconnect** — detects Discord's "Reconnecting" banner, waits, and reloads
- **Human-like timing** — configurable cooldown (default 2.5s) plus random 0.4–0.9s jitter

```python
# All tunables live at the top of the file
CHANNEL_URL        = "https://discord.com/channels/..."
COOLDOWN           = 2.5
AUTOSCROLL_RETRIES = 3
HEADLESS           = False
```

### Autoscroll flow
On each cycle: scroll → try click → if miss, enter retry loop:
```
for attempt in 1..AUTOSCROLL_RETRIES:
    press End → JS scroll to bottom → wait 0.8s → try click
```

* Added a new `logger.js` module that provides a centralized logging system with Python-style formatting, log levels, and support for both the Electron main and renderer processes. File logging is enabled for the main process, and a factory function allows for module-specific loggers.
* Refactored `main.js` to use the new logger throughout, replacing previous `console.log`/`console.error` calls with structured log statements at appropriate log levels. This includes startup, IPC handlers, error handling, and SSH session management, greatly improving debuggability and traceability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR3-R37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR46-R374) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-58417e0f781b6656949d37258c8b9052ed266e2eb7a5163cad7b0863e6b2916aR383-R426)

### Motivation
- Resume checkpoint parsed TODOs could be reintroduced into final sync results even if their source files were deleted on OneDrive, causing deleted TODOs to persist locally.

body:
### Motivation
- Internal WTTJ apply attempts were being blocked by cookie consent overlays (not selector bugs), causing "Could not click internal apply button" failures.
- The goal is to dismiss common overlays (especially Axeptio) and avoid clicking while the page is still hydrating so internal apply clicks succeed reliably.

### Description
- Added a new helper `dismiss_known_blockers(page)` that detects Axeptio (`#axeptio_overlay`) and prefers clicking `#axeptio_btn_dismiss` then `#axeptio_btn_acceptAll`/`#axeptio_main_button`, waits for the overlay to hide/detach, and logs the action. (See `AXEPTIO_*` constants.)

author: austinkennethtucker
body:
🎯 **What:** Fixed a security vulnerability in `src/os/open.zig` where `stderr` output from an OS-level `open()` command (e.g., `xdg-open` or macOS `open`) was logged generically as a warning, exposing raw command URLs and query parameters.
⚠️ **Risk:** If a user interacted with a malicious or otherwise highly sensitive URL that triggered an error during the `open()` command execution (e.g., the browser failed or a schema was unknown), the full raw URL components would be indiscriminately written to the application's debug or standard logs, putting privacy and application security at risk.
🛡️ **Solution:** The resolution disables output collection entirely. `stdout_behavior` and `stderr_behavior` are set to `.Ignore` instead of `.Pipe` prior to `exe.spawn()`. The background `openThread` has been refactored to simply `wait()` for the command execution completion, rather than buffering and reading streams via `collectOutput()`, efficiently mitigating the vulnerability.

author: moltar-bot
body:
## Why
This addresses two failure modes reported in #17:

1. **Provider/model migration dimension mismatch** (e.g. 1536 → 768) can leave a stale `.hnsw` sidecar that loads with incompatible dimensions and causes runtime failures.
2. **Corrupt or malformed index graph edges** can trigger unsafe neighbor index access during search/update paths and bubble up as opaque 500s.

## What changed
### `vectorindex/hnsw.go`
- Added defensive bounds checks for neighbor indices in:
  - `searchLayer`
  - `Remove`
  - `pruneConnections`
- Hardened `Load()` validation:
  - reject invalid dimensions / M / max level / node count / entry index
  - reject dimension mismatch vs configured runtime dimensions
  - validate node id length and layer/connection counts
  - validate every persisted connection index is in bounds
  - handle `nodeCount == 0` cleanly
- Preserve configured dimensions unless unset (instead of blindly overwriting from file).

### `vectorindex/hnsw_test.go`
- Added tests for:
  - dimension mismatch on load
  - invalid neighbor index in persisted file

## Expected effect
- Incompatible/corrupt `.hnsw` now fails fast during load, allowing callers to rebuild index from DB embeddings instead of serving opaque 500s.
- Runtime graph traversals are resilient to bad connection values.

## Notes
- I could not run `go test` locally in this environment because `go`/`gofmt` are not installed on the host path.
- Changes are scoped to vector index load/traversal safety and should be CI-verifiable.

body:
## Summary

- **BREAKING CHANGE**: Remove all automatic PostgreSQL migration hooks (`postgresqlMigration.enabled`, pre-upgrade dump job, post-upgrade restore job, and associated RBAC). The hooks proved too fragile in production — OOM kills on large `query_results` tables, FK constraint violations during restore, and superuser privilege requirements made them unreliable.
- **Remove `postgresqlMigration` values block**: `postgresqlMigration.enabled` and `postgresqlMigration.storage.pvcName` no longer exist. Remove them from your `values.yaml` or `--set` flags before upgrading.
- **Deprecate 3.1.x and 3.2.x**: these versions contained the automatic migration hooks and should not be used for new upgrades.
- **Bump chart to v4.0.0** to signal the breaking change.
- **Document manual migration**: `CHANGELOG.md` now contains a full step-by-step manual PostgreSQL migration runbook (dump → prepare dump → scale down → drop/recreate DB → restore → upgrade → fix FK → run Alembic → scale up), including a known-gotchas table covering every issue encountered during production testing.

## What was removed

| File | Reason |
|---|---|
| `templates/hook-postgres-migration.yaml` | Pre/post-upgrade dump+restore jobs — too fragile |
| `templates/rbac-postgres-migration.yaml` | RBAC only needed by the removed hooks |
| `values.yaml` `postgresqlMigration` block | No longer applicable |

author: gambletan
body:
## Summary

Fixes #13124

`log_validation()` in dreambooth training scripts runs pipeline inference using the same UNet/transformer that is being trained, without `torch.no_grad()`. With `--mixed_precision="fp16"`, gradients are computed and stored during validation inference. When the training loop resumes, the gradient scaler tries to unscale these FP16 gradients, causing:

```
ValueError: Attempting to unscale FP16 gradients.
```

This PR wraps all pipeline inference calls in `log_validation()` with `torch.no_grad()` across **all 17 dreambooth training scripts**, not just the one reported in the issue.

## Changes

- `train_dreambooth.py`
- `train_dreambooth_flux.py`
- `train_dreambooth_sd3.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_flux.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_flux2.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_flux2_img2img.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_flux2_klein.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_flux2_klein_img2img.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_flux_kontext.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_hidream.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_lumina2.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_qwen_image.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_sana.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_sd3.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_sdxl.py`
- `train_dreambooth_lora_z_image.py`

## Root Cause

Validation runs the pipeline which internally calls the UNet/transformer forward pass. Since `torch.no_grad()` is not set, autograd tracks operations and creates FP16 gradient tensors. The `GradScaler` in the training loop then fails because it expects FP32 gradients to unscale.

## Test Plan

- [ ] Verify `train_dreambooth_lora.py` with `--mixed_precision="fp16"` and `--validation_prompt` no longer crashes with `ValueError: Attempting to unscale FP16 gradients`
- [ ] Verify validation images are still generated correctly (inference output is identical with or without `no_grad`)

author: progami
body:
This change fixes two related Talos issues.

First, purchase-order currencies were still inconsistent in a few places even after the UI was updated to treat product and non-freight PO costs as USD. Some non-freight purchase-order API responses could still echo legacy stored GBP values, existing UK PO/manual cost rows still contained historical GBP data, and the create/update paths were not fully enforcing the new rule that purchase orders are always USD while freight may remain USD or GBP.

Second, the dashboard inventory levels graph did not offer an all-time view. The existing range picker only supported fixed recent periods and always sent explicit start and end dates, so there was no way to ask the stats route for a complete inventory history.

The fix normalizes the non-freight purchase-order stack around USD. Supplier adjustment and warehouse-cost responses now return USD consistently, the manufacturing purchase-order detail payload does the same for supplier adjustments, PO line updates always rewrite touched lines to USD, and new PO creation now explicitly requires USD for line currency input. I also added a targeted data backfill script and script entry to normalize legacy purchase-order line and manual PO financial rows to USD while intentionally preserving freight GBP rows. That backfill was executed against the UK main and dev schemas.

For the dashboard, the range picker now includes an All Time option. The page omits explicit dates for that selection, and the dashboard stats route detects all-time requests by deriving the earliest inventory transaction date in scope and building the inventory graph from that point forward.

Validation included targeted eslint on the changed Talos files, `pnpm --filter @targon/talos type-check:app`, the currency backfill dry run plus apply, and direct SQL verification confirming that PO line and manual PO-cost GBP rows are now zero while freight GBP rows remain intact.

author: flvndvd
body: ## Description Agent-loop workers have been OOMing in production. Heap snapshot analysis revealed that `lru-memoizer` caches in `isDeepDiveDisabledByAdmin` and `getFeatureFlags` were growing unbounded, retaining ~25% of the heap (203 MB in a single snapshot). ## Root cause Both memoizers used `memoizer.sync()` with an async load function. `memoizer.sync` caches the return value of load directly which for an async function is a `Promise` object, not the resolved value. Each Promise carries a `` (the Node.js async context from dd-trace and Temporal), retaining spans, activity contexts, and associated data. Combined with missing max options, the cache grew unbounded. `itemMaxAge: 3000` (3s TTL) only triggers lazy eviction on access, so entries for workspaces that are never re-accessed stayed forever. Heap snapshot retainer chain: ``` LRUCache (symbol cache) → 203 MB (25% of heap) -> result() (memoized function) → 203 MB -> isDeepDiveDisabledByAdmin in system / Context → 266 MB (33%) -> Timeout (300s timer, EventCoalescer cleanup interval) -> timerListMap in system / Context (root) ``` ## Fix - Switch from `memoizer.sync` to the callback-based memoizer API. The callback API stores the resolved value (a boolean / string array) in the cache, not thePromise. Eliminating the async context retention entirely. - Add max: 100 to bound the cache and prevent unbounded growth from lazy TTL eviction. ## Reproduction ``` === LRU Cache Implementation Test === --- OLD: memoizer.sync with async load --- First call return type : object Is a Promise? : true Same reference (cached): true Resolved value : true Resolved type : boolean --- NEW: callback-based memoizer --- First call resolved : true Resolved type : boolean Is a Promise? : false Second call resolved : true Same value (cached) : true --- Memory impact comparison --- Entries cached : 1000 Old (Promise) heap delta: 1624.8 KB New (boolean) heap delta : -1216.9 KB --- Assertions --- PASS: old cache stores Promise objects PASS: new cache stores resolved values (not Promises) All checks passed. ``` ## Tests ## Risk ## Deploy Plan

through Rube MCP operator flows.

- add six archetype prompt workflow docs covering research, docs-grounded answers, Linear triage,

body:
# Description

Fix naive `str.replace("FROM ", ...)` in `SQLDatabase.run_sql()` that incorrectly schema-prefixes CTE (Common Table Expression) names, breaking queries like:

```sql
WITH my_cte AS (SELECT * FROM users) SELECT * FROM my_cte
-- Before (broken): ... SELECT * FROM myschema.my_cte
-- After (fixed):   ... SELECT * FROM my_cte
```

Replace with regex-based `_add_schema_prefix()` method that:
1. Extracts CTE names from `WITH [RECURSIVE] name AS (` clauses (including comma-separated CTEs)
2. Uses regex to match `FROM`/`JOIN` table references
3. Skips CTE names and already schema-qualified identifiers when prefixing

Fixes #19889

body:
## Summary

- **Navigation history**: `useNavigationTracker` now records full URLs (`pathname + searchStr`) in sessionStorage. When URL params change on the same page, the last history entry is updated in place rather than appending a new one.
- **Back navigation**: `goBack()` in `useAppNavigation` uses `router.history.push(fullUrl)` so the exact URL — including `?q=`, `?tags=1`, `?filters=1` etc — is restored when returning from an item detail page.
- **Cross-page carry-over removed**: `useUrlSearchAndFilters` no longer seeds or saves to `item-list-search-prefs` in sessionStorage. Each list page's filter/search state is now fully independent, preserved only via URL.
- **Sort persistence**: Pantry migrated from `sessionStorage.ts` (deprecated) to `useSortFilter('pantry')`, consistent with all other list pages.
- **Scroll restoration**: New `useScrollRestoration(key)` hook saves `window.scrollY` on unmount and restores it after all layout-affecting data loads (items + tags + tagTypes + vendors + recipes). Wired into all 7 list pages (pantry, shopping, tag/vendor/recipe item tabs, tag list, vendor list).
- **Bug fix**: `useScrollRestoration` captures scroll in the render phase (before DOM commit) to work around TanStack Router updating `useRouterState` before unmounting, which would otherwise shrink the page (tags hidden) and clamp `window.scrollY` before the save.
- **Search row fix**: `ItemListToolbar` adds a `useEffect` so the search input row opens automatically when navigating back to a URL that already has `?q=`.
- **Cleanup**: Removed unused `saveFilters`, `loadFilters`, `saveUiPrefs`, `loadUiPrefs`, `saveSortPrefs`, `loadSortPrefs` exports from `lib/sessionStorage.ts`.

author: copilot
body:
Adds a second rendering backend implementing stochastic transparency for Gaussian splatting ([arXiv 2503.24366](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.24366)) using only PyTorch built-ins — no C++/CUDA extensions required. Selectable at runtime via `--renderer stochastic`.

## Algorithm

**Forward pass** — tile-based; for each tile:
1. Project Gaussians to 2D (Jacobian-based perspective covariance, same convention as the CUDA renderer).
2. Compute per-(Gaussian, pixel) alpha values: `α_i(p) = opacity_i · exp(-0.5 · dᵀ Σ⁻¹ d)`.
3. Derive alpha-compositing weights `w_i = α_i · T_i` where `T_i = ∏_{j<i}(1 - α_j)`.
4. Draw S independent samples per pixel via the **Gumbel-max trick** on `(w_0, …, w_{M-1}, w_bg)`. Expected value equals standard alpha compositing (unbiased estimator).

**Backward pass** — straight-through estimator: gradients propagate through the closed-form expected-value formula (alpha compositing), not through the discrete sample selection step. The `screenspace_points` add-zero trick preserves compatibility with the training loop's densification logic.

## Changes

- **`gaussian_renderer/stochastic_renderer.py`** *(new)* — `StochasticTransparencyRenderer` class with `.render()` returning the same dict as the original renderer. Handles 3D/4D Gaussians, temporal opacity, SH colour evaluation, and tile-based assembly via `torch.cat` (fully differentiable, no in-place graph breaks).

- **`gaussian_renderer/__init__.py`** — `render()` dispatches to the stochastic backend when `pipe.renderer == "stochastic"`; original CUDA path unchanged.

- **`arguments/__init__.py`** — three new `PipelineParams` fields: `renderer`, `num_samples`, `tile_size`.

## Usage

```bash
# Training with stochastic renderer, 16 samples/pixel
python train.py --config configs/dnerf/lego.yaml --renderer stochastic --num_samples 16

# Inference
python render.py -m output/lego --renderer stochastic --num_samples 32
```

Higher `--num_samples` reduces Monte Carlo noise; `--num_samples 1` is fastest but noisiest. The default (`--renderer original`) is unchanged.

author: tktcorporation
body:
## Summary
Fixes EACCES errors that occur when giget attempts to write to the cache directory in environments with restricted permissions (e.g., GitHub Codespaces).

## Changes
- Added `ensureGigetCacheDir()` function that:
  - Checks if the default giget cache directory (`~/.cache`) is writable
  - Falls back to using the OS temporary directory by setting `XDG_CACHE_HOME` if the default cache directory is not writable
  - Respects existing `XDG_CACHE_HOME` environment variable if already set
  
- Integrated the cache directory check into two key functions:
  - `downloadTemplateToTemp()` - called before downloading templates
  - `fetchTemplates()` - called before fetching templates during the download flow

- Updated imports to include necessary utilities:
  - `accessSync` and `constants` from `node:fs` for permission checking
  - `homedir` and `tmpdir` from `node:os` for directory resolution
  - `resolve` from `pathe` for path resolution

## Implementation Details
The solution leverages giget's built-in support for the `XDG_CACHE_HOME` environment variable. When the default cache directory is not writable, we set `XDG_CACHE_HOME` to point to the OS temporary directory, allowing giget to use an alternative writable location without code changes to giget itself.

author: bragaigor
body:
Adds a new helper function CalcBlobFeeWithConfig that calculates the blob base fee from a params.BlobConfig directly, without requiring a full params.ChainConfig.

The existing CalcBlobFee function requires a `*params.ChainConfig` and a `*types.Header`, then internally resolves the active blob schedule via `latestBlobConfig(config, header.Time)`. This works well when the caller has a complete chain config, but Nitro's ParentChain component now fetches the blob schedule dynamically from the parent chain's `eth_config` RPC (EIP-7910), yielding a standalone `*params.BlobConfig` rather than a full chain config.

Without this helper, the caller would need to either:

- Reconstruct a full `ChainConfig` just to call `CalcBlobFee` (wasteful and error-prone)
- Duplicate the `blobBaseFee` calculation logic outside of geth (breaks encapsulation)


pulled in by https://github.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/pull/4511
part of [NIT-4354](https://linear.app/offchain-labs/issue/NIT-4354/use-eth-config-rpc-method-to-get-bpo-parameters-of-parent-chain)

author: elfenlieds7
body:
## Summary
- **LLMBlobTransport**: Thread-safe in-memory BlobTransport for CAS blob storage (satisfies BlobTransport Protocol)
- **OpenAICompatibleBackend**: CASBackend subclass registered as `"openai_compatible"` connector (category=`"compute"`)
  - `write_content()` stores request JSON in CAS, calls LLM API, stores response, returns session envelope hash
  - Session envelope links `request_hash` + `response_hash` (all CAS-addressed)
  - OpenAI SDK as universal transport (SudoRouter, OpenRouter, Ollama, local LLMs)
- 27 unit tests with fully mocked OpenAI API

## Design
Step 1 of the LLM backend driver plan (Task #1589):
1. ~~Step 0: CDC Promotion (#1681)~~ — merged via PR #3086
2. **Step 1: Sync MVP** — this PR
3. Step 2: DT_STREAM Streaming + CAS Flush (next)
4. Step 3: MessageBoundaryStrategy (chunking)
5. Step 4: AgentService Integration

## Usage
```python
# Mount at any VFS path
nexus mount /zone/llm/openai --backend=openai_compatible \
    --config='{"base_url":"https://api.sudorouter.ai","api_key":"sk-..."}'

# Or programmatically
backend = OpenAICompatibleBackend(
    base_url="https://api.openai.com/v1",
    api_key="sk-...",
    default_model="gpt-4o",
)
result = backend.write_content(json.dumps({
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]
}).encode())
session = json.loads(backend.read_content(result.content_hash))
response = json.loads(backend.read_content(session["response_hash"]))
```

- [x] OpenAICompatibleBackend: write+read session, request/response CAS, custom model, extra params, error handling (13 tests)
- [x] ruff lint + format clean

body:
### Motivation
- Allow the PMF explorer to accept polynomial expressions (single-letter variable) in the `x` column as well as in `p(x)` so the plotted support, E[X], validation, and tooltips reflect evaluated numeric values at the chosen variable value.
- Enforce the existing requirement of at most one variable name across the whole PMF and keep the current UI/UX and plotting behavior intact.

### Description
- Generalized the expression parser/evaluator into `analyzeExpression(raw, label)` and `evaluateParsedExpression(parsed, v)` so both `x` and `p(x)` support the same numeric and polynomial syntax and same validation rules (added to `grade10/src/pages/g10-t3-discrete-probabilities.html`).
- Refactored input parsing into `parseEntries(...)` and `evaluateEntries(...)` and added `collectDetectedVariables(...)` so variables are discovered across both `x` and `p(x)`, the single-variable rule is enforced across the full input, and evaluation happens before validation/plotting.
- Changed duplicate detection and support set generation to use evaluated numeric `x` values instead of raw tokens so expressions that collapse to the same numeric value at the current variable are flagged as duplicates and the support set shows evaluated numbers.
- Preserved dragging behavior for rows with raw numeric `x` by tagging plotted points with `isXRawNumeric` and disabling drag for symbolic `x` rows (point meta now includes `draggable`), and kept existing UI, graph, toggle, slider, and tooltip display (tooltips show evaluated numeric pairs).
- Minor messaging tweaks to error/graph text to clarify expression-based inputs and updated multi-variable validation text to mention both `x` and `p(x)`.

### Testing
- Syntax check: extracted the in-page script and ran `node --check /tmp/g10_pmf.js` to verify JavaScript parses without syntax errors, which succeeded.
- Integration attempt: attempted automated UI verification via Playwright to exercise table/text modes and the variable slider, but Playwright browser launches failed in this environment (Chromium crashed and Firefox returned network errors), so no browser-run assertions or screenshots were produced.

author: alexskrypnyk
body:
## Summary

Code simplification and cleanup across `src/` — reduces duplication, fixes bugs, inlines single-use variables, and improves readability.

### Bug fixes

- **MinkContext**: Fixed `ajax_timeout` using `||` instead of `??`, which always evaluated to `1` (boolean `true`) instead of the configured timeout value.
- **ConfigContext**: Fixed double `json_decode()` call — the value was decoded twice per row (once without `TRUE` for the truthiness check, once with `TRUE` for the actual value).
- **RawDrupalContext**: Fixed `alterNodeParameters()` calling `getDriver()` twice instead of reusing the `$driver` variable already in scope.
- **DrupalContext**: Fixed `assertLoggedInByName()` calling `getUser()` twice and redundantly calling `setCurrentUser()` (already done by `login()`).

### Code deduplication

- **RegionTrait** (new): Extracted `getRegion()` from identical implementations in `MinkContext` and `MarkupContext`.
- **`getDrupalTranslationResources()`**: Centralised the `glob()` call for translation resources in `RawDrupalContext`; 4 subclasses now delegate instead of inlining the same path.
- **`createAndLoginUserWithRole()`**: Unified two near-identical user creation + login blocks in `DrupalContext`.
- **`createUserStub()`**: Extracted user object construction (name/pass/mail) shared by `createAndLoginUserWithRole()` and `assertLoggedInWithPermissions()`.
- **`hasSendMailTag()`**: Extracted duplicated tag-merge + check logic from `disableMail()` and `enableMail()` in `MailContext`.
- **`findElementByText()`**: Extracted duplicated element-search loop from two methods in `MarkupContext`.

### Simplifications

- **`dispatchHooks()`**: Now receives a FQCN via `::class` instead of building it with string concatenation.
- **`cleanLanguages()`**: Replaced per-item `unset()` inside a loop with `$this->languages = []` after the loop.
- **`loadParameters()`** (ServiceContainer): Removed identity-copy foreach loop; passes `$config` directly.
- **`sortMessages()`** (RawMailContext): Collapsed 3 `array_key_exists` blocks into `+= [defaults]` and replaced manual column extraction with `array_column()`.
- **`filterMatches()`** (EntityHook): Removed dead variable assignment in Yoda condition.
- **MinkContext**: Combined 6 separate heading CSS queries (`h1`..`h6`) into a single `findAll('css', 'h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6')` selector in 3 methods. Used `$buttonObj->press()` instead of double `findButton()` lookup.
- **MarkupContext**: Inlined single-use `$regionObj`, `$buttonObj`, `$elements` variables. Removed redundant `!empty()` guards before `foreach`. Used early returns to flatten nested conditionals. Fixed `$attrfound` → `$attrFound` casing.
- **MinkContext**: Inlined single-use intermediary variables (`$element`, `$regionObj`, `$regionText`, `$result`) in 16 methods. Fixed `$radiobutton` → `$radioButton` and `$labelonpage` → `$labelOnPage` casing. Collapsed `regionFillField()` from 4 lines to 1.
- **MessageContext**: Inlined single-use `$selector` variable. Removed unnecessary `!empty()` guard wrapping `foreach` in `assertNot()`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `ahoy test-phpspec` — 77 examples pass
- [ ] `ahoy test-unit` — 276 tests pass
- [ ] `ahoy test-bdd` — all profiles pass (4 pre-existing failures unrelated to these changes)

author: 9clg6
body:
## Summary
Move all state mutations inside `setState()` callbacks instead of mutating before calling empty `setState(() {})`. Remove redundant `setState()` calls and simplify control flow.

## PR Chain (Performance Optimization Series)
```
PR1 ← main
PR2 ← PR1            ← YOU ARE HERE
PR3 ← PR2     PR4 ← PR2     PR5 ← PR2
       \         |
        PR6 ← PR3 + PR4
              |
             PR7 ← PR6
```
Depends on: #2919

## Changes
- **9 files** with setState hygiene fixes
- State mutations moved inside callbacks in: `tom_bootstrap_dialog`, `key_verification_dialog`, `login`, `homeserver_picker`, `add_widget_tile`, `media_viewer`, `chat_settings_popup_menu`, `mxc_image`
- Import reordering in `matrix.dart` and `homeserver_picker.dart`
- Redundant switch-case removed in `homeserver_picker.dart`

## Why
Empty `setState(() {})` is a code smell — Flutter still schedules a rebuild, but the intent is unclear. Moving mutations inside the callback makes the relationship between state change and rebuild explicit, and prevents bugs where mutations happen but `setState` is never reached (e.g., early return).

author: copilot
body:
The system had a Flask web UI but no visibility into how scores were computed — only a single aggregate match score was shown. Users also requested elaboration on the technologies in use.

## Score breakdown — backend + frontend

`MatchResult` now carries three per-component scores and preferred-skill detail:

```python
@dataclass
class MatchResult:
    ...
    req_score: float = 0.0          # required-skills coverage (0–1)
    pref_score: float = 0.0         # preferred-skills coverage (0–1)
    exp_score: float = 0.0          # experience adequacy (0–1)
    preferred_matched: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    preferred_missing: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
```

A new `_component_scores()` helper in `matcher.py` computes all fields in one pass, eliminating the duplicate `_skill_overlap` calls that existed in both `match_application()` and `rank_applications()`.

## UI changes

- **`/results`** — four score columns (Total, Required 60%, Preferred 20%, Experience 20%), each with a mini progress bar; matched skills shown as green badges, missing skills as struck-through red/grey badges; formula banner; live text search; "View JSON" link to `/api/results`
- **`/jobs/<id>`** — same four-column breakdown applied to the ranked applicants table
- **`/about`** (new) — full tech stack reference: Python 3, Flask 3, Jinja2, Bootstrap 5, Bootstrap Icons, Vanilla JS, JSON storage, rotating logger, pytest; scoring formula with weights; threshold config; pipeline diagram; API endpoint table with live links

## REST API

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/results` | All match results with full `score_breakdown` per component (score, weight, weighted contribution, matched/missing skills) |
| `GET /api/jobs` | All job postings |
| `GET /api/applications` | All applications |

## Security

`app.run(debug=True)` replaced with env-variable control:
```python
debug_mode = os.environ.get("FLASK_DEBUG", "false").lower() == "true"
app.run(debug=debug_mode, ...)
```

author: tomas-stefano
body:
## Summary

- Fix `NoMethodError: undefined method 'parameterize' for an instance of ActionController::Parameters` caused by malformed requests sending `location` as a hash instead of a string
- Guard `location` params in `ResultsController`, `CoursesController`, and `SavedCoursesController` to reject non-string values at the controller level
- Guard `page` param in `ResultsController` against non-string/non-numeric values
- Handle `ArgumentError` in `FeedbacksController` gracefully
- Add controller spec reproducing the location hash param error

## Context

When a request sends `location` as a nested hash (e.g., `?location[foo]=bar`), `params[:location]` returns an `ActionController::Parameters` object instead of a String. This propagates to `Geolocation::AddressResolver#cache_key` which calls `.parameterize` — a String-only method — causing a 500 error.

The fix rejects non-string values early at the controller boundary rather than coercing with `.to_s`, which would mask invalid input and make unnecessary API calls.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `GET /results?location[foo]=bar` no longer raises a 500
- [ ] Verify `GET /results?location=London` still works as expected
- [ ] Verify `GET /results?page[foo]=bar` returns page 1 gracefully
- [ ] Run controller specs

author: pgrayy
body:
## Description

Multi-agent orchestration nodes (`AgentNode`, `Graph`, `Swarm`) previously required the concrete `Agent` class, preventing custom `AgentBase` implementations (such as `A2AAgent` or user-defined agents) from participating in orchestration.

## Motivation

`AgentBase` is the polymorphic interface for all agent types, but the multi-agent system was coupled to the concrete `Agent` class. This meant only `Agent` instances could be used as nodes in `Graph` and `Swarm` orchestrators. Any `AgentBase` implementor should be able to participate in multi-agent workflows.

## Public API Changes

`AgentNode`, `NodeDefinition`, and `SwarmNodeDefinition` now accept `AgentBase` instead of `Agent`:

```typescript
// Before: only concrete Agent accepted
const graph = new Graph({
  nodes: [agent], // agent must be instanceof Agent
  edges: [...],
})

// After: any AgentBase implementation works
const graph = new Graph({
  nodes: [a2aAgent, customAgent], // any AgentBase
  edges: [...],
})
```

`AgentBase` and `MultiAgentBase` now include a `type` discriminator field (`"agent"` and `"multiAgent"` respectively), enabling type-safe narrowing in union types like `NodeDefinition` without relying on `instanceof`:

```typescript
interface AgentBase {
  readonly type: 'agent'
  // ...
}

interface MultiAgentBase {
  readonly type: 'multiAgent'
  // ...
}
```

`NodeDefinition` is simplified to use these discriminators directly:

```typescript
// Before
type NodeDefinition =
  | Agent
  | MultiAgentBase
  | Node
  | (AgentNodeOptions & { type: 'agent' })
  | (MultiAgentNodeOptions & { type: 'multiAgent' })

// After
type NodeDefinition = AgentBase | MultiAgentBase | Node | AgentNodeOptions | MultiAgentNodeOptions
```

Snapshot/restore in `AgentNode.handle()` is now conditional, only applying when the wrapped agent is an `Agent` instance (since `AgentBase` does not expose snapshot internals).

## Breaking Changes

Adding `readonly type: 'agent'` to `AgentBase` and `readonly type: 'multiAgent'` to `MultiAgentBase` is a breaking change for any external implementations of these interfaces. Existing implementations will need to add the `type` field:

```typescript
// Before
class MyAgent implements AgentBase {
  readonly id = 'my-agent'
  // ...
}

// After
class MyAgent implements AgentBase {
  readonly type = 'agent' as const
  readonly id = 'my-agent'
  // ...
}
```

## Documentation

No documentation updates needed at this time. `AgentBase` documentation is planned once the interface design is finalized (there are open considerations around how `AgentBase` and `AgentData` interact).

We do have documentation for passing an A2AAgent into Graph in the works under https://github.com/strands-agents/docs/pull/658, waiting on these changes so the PR CI will pass.

## Related Issues

N/A

Breaking change

- [x] I have added any necessary tests that prove my fix is effective or my feature works
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly

author: copilot
body:
Synced subtitles used `ref.start_ms + tgt.duration_ms` for `end_ms`, preserving the target's (wrong) duration instead of the reference's (correct) timing. This causes subtitles to display too briefly when the target has shorter durations. Progress reporting only showed task names with no granularity into what was actually happening.

### Timing fix (`sync_engine.py`)

All three sync paths (`sync_by_sequence`, `sync_by_similarity`, `sync_to_transcript`) now take `end_ms` from the reference/transcript segment, not the target duration:

```python
# Before
end_ms=ref.start_ms + tgt.duration_ms

# After
end_ms=ref.end_ms
```

### Audio extraction progress (`audio_extractor.py`)

- Query duration via `ffprobe`, then run ffmpeg with `-progress pipe:1`
- Parse `out_time_us` from machine-readable progress stream via `Popen`
- Report real-time percentage: `"Extracting audio: 45% — 90s / 200s"`

### Whisper transcription progress (`whisper_transcriber.py`)

- Set `verbose=True` on `model.transcribe()` and intercept stdout via `_ProgressWriter`
- Forward each decoded segment to the progress callback as it's produced
- Users see `"Whisper: [00:00.000 --> 00:05.000] Hello world"` in real-time instead of silence during the blocking transcribe call

author: darth-sipid
body:
Port 587 had ssl=yes on the listener, forcing implicit TLS when it should use STARTTLS (plaintext connection that upgrades). Removed the ssl=yes so Dovecot offers STARTTLS instead.

The ssl_cert was pointing at the leaf certificate only, without intermediates. Clients couldn't verify the chain and closed the connection during handshake. Now concatenates leaf + CA bundle into a full chain file. Also adds ssl=required and ssl_min_protocol=TLSv1.2.

author: timoangerer
body:
Implements a standalone 2D top-down debug visualization for the plot generator. Users can inspect plot layouts, row assignments, and street layout in real-time with an interactive control panel for adjusting PlotConfig parameters.

**Key features:**
- HTML Canvas 2D rendering with row-based color coding (warm oranges for Row A, cool blues for Row B)
- Interactive control panel for seed, street dimensions, and plot dimensions
- Pan/zoom navigation with stable viewport (view only auto-fits on initial load)
- Separate entry point: `npm run dev:plot-lab`

**Changes:**
- `plot-lab.html`, `vite.plot-lab.config.ts`: Standalone entry point setup
- `src/plot-lab/viewer/main.tsx`: React app wiring config state and plot generation
- `src/plot-lab/viewer/plot-canvas.tsx`: Canvas 2D renderer with coordinate mapping, auto-fit, pan/zoom
- `src/plot-lab/viewer/control-panel.tsx`: Tailwind control panel for PlotConfig fields
- `openspec/specs/plot-lab/spec.md`: Specification for the plot-lab capability
- `openspec/specs/env-lab/spec.md`: Reformatted spec with proper requirement structure

author: guiimoreira
body:
### Motivation
- Permitir recuperação de partidas após reinício do servidor mantendo um snapshot mínimo do estado no Firestore para reconexão dos jogadores. 
- Evitar perda definitiva de partidas ao encerrar mover jogos finalizados para histórico (`partidas_historico`) e remover de `partidas_ativas`. 
- Detectar e limpar partidas abandonadas automaticamente usando uma janela TTL para reduzir custo e lixo no banco. 
- Documentar custo/performance e limites operacionais para orientar uso em produção (limite de 1 MiB por documento, writes por ação, etc.).

### Description
- Adicionadas helpers em `sockets/manager.js`: `montarSnapshotPartida`, `persistirPartidaAtiva`, `moverPartidaParaHistorico`, `carregarPartidasRecuperaveis`, `limparPartidasAbandonadas` e `iniciarLimpezaPeriodica` para gerenciar snapshot e TTL. 
- Persistência integrada ao fluxo de jogo: snapshot inicial ao criar a partida, gravação após cada ação válida (`passar_turno`, `jogar_carta`, `atacar_fortaleza`, `declarar_ataque`), e atualização em reconexão/desconexão. 
- Ao encerrar partida, o snapshot final é copiado para `partidas_historico` e o documento é removido de `partidas_ativas`. 
- Startup refatorado em `server.js` para `bootstrap()` assíncrono que chama `carregarPartidasRecuperaveis` e `iniciarLimpezaPeriodica` antes de registrar os sockets. 
- Adicionada documentação em `README.md` com schema mínimo de `partidas_ativas` (`sala`, `estado`, `jogadores`, `updatedAt`), fluxo de persistência, política TTL/limpeza e considerações de custo/performance e limite de tamanho do documento. 

### Testing
- Executado `npm test` e todos os testes unitários em `tests/*.test.js` passaram (4/4 passando). 
- Executado `node --check server.js` e `node --check sockets/manager.js` sem erros de sintaxe. 
- Validações de integração com Firestore não foram executadas aqui; funções usam a API `db.collection(...).doc(...).set/delete/get` e podem requerer credenciais válidas em ambiente de staging/produção para testes end-to-end.

------

author: seongeun308
body:
## Summary > 이 `PR`에서 `제공`하는 `솔루션`과 그 `설계 의도`를 설명해 주세요. _( like 흑백요리사 )_ > `변경사항`이 필요한 이유, 즉 `컨텍스트` 와 해결하려는 `문제의 핵심`을 `요약`하고, `리뷰어`가 `어떤 관점`에서 봐줬으면 좋겠는지 명시해주세요. 기존 펀딩 참여 주문 생성 과정에서 fundingId를 기반으로 펀딩 API이 아닌 잘못된 위시리스트 API 요청으로 이어지던 문제를 수정하고, 주문 생성 로직의 응집도를 높이기 위한 리팩토링을 진행했습니다. 리뷰어분들은 아래 목록을 중점적으로 봐주시면 좋겠습니다. - ReqeustBody 객체가 변경된 점 - Wishlist API 요청을 제거한 점 - Product API 요청을 추가한 점 - 파사드 내 직접 호출이 아닌 FundingQueryPort를 활용한 점 - TargetType 추가 및 변경된 점 --- ## What's Changed > `PR`에서 `변경되는 점`들을 설명해 주세요. `UI 변경`이 있다면 `스크린샷`을 첨부해주세요. ### 테스트 케이스 추가 및 강화 - `TargetIdResolver` 및 `TargetTypeResolver` 단위 테스트 추가 - DIRECT_PURCHASE, GIFT, FUNDING 등 도메인별 시나리오 및 예외 정책 검증 ### 상품 스냅샷 및 주문 생성 로직 수정 - 불필요한 위시리스트 API 호출을 제거하고 `productId`, `wishlistItemId` 기반으로 로직 정정 - `productId`로 상품 정보를 `wishlistItemId` 펀딩 정보를 요청 - 외부 API 연동을 위한 `ProductSnapshot` 및 `ProductClient` 도입 - `TargetType` ENUM 확장 및 판별 메커니즘 추가 ### DTO 및 Command 구조 개선 - 기존 Adpater인 `PlaceOrderItemRequest`를 Application인 `PlaceOrderCommand` 에서 호출하는 문제 존재 - `PlaceOrderItemCommand`를 생성해 헥사고날에 맞게 수정 - 파사드와 주문 도메인에서 `PlaceOrderCommand` 중복 이름으로 파사드에서 펀딩 참여를 위한 전용 커맨드를 `ParticipateFundingItemCommand`로 이름 수정 ### 구성 요소 명칭 및 역할 정립 - CreateOrderCommand → PlaceOrderCommand 등 명칭 변경을 통한 의미 명확화 - OrderController 및 OrderService를 리팩토링된 구조에 맞게 업데이트 --- ## Decisions & Trade-offs > 개발중에 추가로 고려한 부분에 대해서 공유해주세요. 예를 들어,
> `A 방식 대신 B 방식을 선택한 이유`나, `성능` 혹은 `사용자 경험`을 위해 고민한 흔적을 남겨주세요. #### 1. 모든 주문 항목이 일반 구매일 경우 `FundingQueryPort`를 호출하지 않음 - 빈 객체로 대체해 불필요한 API를 줄임 #### 2. 요청 객체 내 `productId`, `wishlistItemId`, `fundingId` 명시적 분리 - 기존에는 targetId라는 단일 필드에 의존하여 OrderItemType에 따라 그 의미를 다르게 해석 - **모호한 식별자**: targetId가 구체적으로 무엇을 의미하는지 알 수 없어, 비즈니스 로직이 OrderItemType 강결합 - **데이터 접근 제약**: 펀딩 참여 주문의 경우 targetId가 fundingId로 쓰이는데, 이 과정에서 상품 정보를 조회하기 위한 식별자가 누락되어 API 호출 불가능 - 이를 해결하기 위해 목적별 필드 분리 - `productId`: 상품 정보 조회를 위한 단일 창구로 활용 - `wishlistItemId`: 위시리스트 및 연관 펀딩 정보 조회를 위한 키로 활용 - `fundingId`: 기존 펀딩 참여 시 명확한 식별자로 활용 --- ## Future Improvements > 이번 `PR`의 `범위`에는 포함되지 않았지만, 추후 `고도화`하거나 `보완`하고 싶은 점이 있다면 적어주세요. > 예를 들어, 남겨둔 `기술 부채`나 `최적화` 계획, 혹은 `확장성`을 위해 다음 단계에서 `시도해 볼 만한 아이디어`를 공유해주세요. --- ### Linked Issues - closes #426

author: groenbech96
body:
## Summary
- Enables AL-Go `incrementalBuilds` in `.github/AL-Go-Settings.json` with `modifiedApps` mode
- Only rebuilds apps whose source files changed (plus their dependency chain), instead of rebuilding entire projects
- Applies to both CI/CD push builds and PR builds, significantly reducing build times for the ~329 apps in this repo

## Configuration added
```json
"incrementalBuilds": {
  "onPush": false,
  "onPull_Request": true,
  "onSchedule": false,
  "retentionDays": 30,
  "mode": "modifiedApps"
}
```

## How it works
1. AL-Go finds the latest successful CI/CD build within 30 days as a baseline
2. Compares changed files between current commit and baseline
3. Only rebuilds modified apps and their dependents
4. Reuses pre-built artifacts from the baseline for unchanged apps
5. Falls back to full build if no valid baseline exists or if `fullBuildPatterns` match

## Safety
- Changes to `build/*`, `src/rulesets/*`, and critical workflow files still trigger full rebuilds (via existing `fullBuildPatterns`)
- If no baseline build is found within `retentionDays`, a full build runs automatically

author: froquede
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive enhancement of the HTML+CSS → Unity UI Toolkit converter, inspired by the work in [floatingsnowflake/html2uuitk@7235b3a](https://github.com/floatingsnowflake/html2uuitk/commit/7235b3a). That commit introduced valuable improvements but as a single massive change (+4,821 lines) with bugs and Chinese-only docs. This PR extracts the good parts, fixes the issues, and adds new features — all in clean, incremental commits.

### What's included (6 commits):

1. **Test infrastructure** — 158 unit tests using Node.js native test runner
2. **Bug fixes** — input type null safety, letter-spacing regex hardening, unmapped asset handling
3. **Modularization** — monolithic `index.js` split into 6 focused `src/` modules with `ctx` object pattern (no more global mutable state) and async/await file I/O
4. **Feature enhancements** (from floatingsnowflake):
   - 20+ new HTML tag mappings (button, select, textarea, img, progress, semantic HTML5, input types)
   - Font shorthand parsing, font-style/weight → `-unity-font-style`
   - Background/border shorthand parsing
   - Border-radius expansion, display/overflow/position value mapping
   - htmlOnlyElements filtering, uxmlSkipTags for UXML, expanded breaking selectors
   - Enable opacity, rotate, scale, translate, transform-origin as native USS properties
   - Strip `inherit` values and CSS-only `cursor` property
   - rem/em → px conversion, modern rgb()/hsl() space-syntax support
5. **Bug fixes for floatingsnowflake's code** — duplicate USS output, redundant mapped selectors (`Label, Label, Label`)
6. **New features beyond floatingsnowflake**:
   - margin/padding shorthand expansion (`margin: 10px 20px` → individual properties)
   - box-shadow → USS shadow custom properties
   - Pseudo-class support (`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus` pass through to USS)
   - CSS `var()` fallback syntax (`var(--color, red)`)

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 158 tests passing, 0 failures
- [x] End-to-end manual test: HTML with div, h1, button, input, checkbox, nav, svg + CSS with body, margin shorthand, display:block, font-weight, border-radius, :hover, :active, opacity, scale, table → correct UXML/USS output
- [x] SVG filtered from UXML, table filtered from USS
- [x] Input without type defaults to ui:TextField (no crash)
- [x] No duplicate rules in USS output

body:
## Summary

Fixes #463

The label `app.kubernetes.io/name` was hardcoded directly in the `labels` block of all 5 resources (ServiceAccount, Role ×2, RoleBinding ×2) in `k8s-pipeline-rbac.yaml`, while the included `OpenMetadata.labels` helper already emits the same key via `OpenMetadata.selectorLabels`. This produced a duplicate YAML mapping key, causing `helm install`/`helm upgrade` failures on OpenShift and EKS when using the K8sPipelineClient (`type: k8s`):

```
line 11: mapping key "app.kubernetes.io/name" already defined at line 8
```

**Fix:** Remove the 5 hardcoded `app.kubernetes.io/name: openmetadata` lines and let the value flow correctly through the `OpenMetadata.labels` helper. The `app.kubernetes.io/component` label (`ingestion`/`server`) is preserved as it is not emitted by the helper.

## Changes

- `charts/openmetadata/templates/k8s-pipeline-rbac.yaml` — removed hardcoded `app.kubernetes.io/name: openmetadata` from all 5 resource label blocks (lines 11, 25, 56, 75, 121)

## Additional finding

The hardcoded label was also **wrong** when `nameOverride` is set — `main` produced two conflicting values (`openmetadata` + the override) in the same labels block. The fix makes the label correctly reflect `nameOverride`.

## Test plan

- [x] `helm lint charts/openmetadata --values charts/openmetadata/values.yaml` — 0 failures
- [x] `helm lint` with `pipelineServiceClientConfig.type=k8s` and `rbac.enabled=true` — 0 failures

- [x] Python strict YAML duplicate-key parser — 5 documents, 0 duplicate keys
- [x] **Go `gopkg.in/yaml.v2` with `SetStrict(true)`** (exact library used by Flux helm-controller) — bug reproduced on `main`, clean pass on fix branch
- [x] `nameOverride` edge case — label correctly reflects override value

author: 9clg6
body:
## Summary
Fix stream subscription leaks and add filtering to reduce unnecessary listener callbacks.

## PR Chain (Performance Optimization Series)
```
PR1 ← main
PR2 ← PR1
PR3 ← PR2            ← YOU ARE HERE
PR4 ← PR2     PR5 ← PR2
       \         |
        PR6 ← PR3 + PR4
              |
             PR7 ← PR6
```
Depends on: #2920

## Changes

### Subscription leaks fixed
- **`matrix.dart`**: Track `onToDeviceEvent` and `onUiaRequest` subscriptions, cancel them in `_cancelSubs()` and `dispose()`
- **`matrix.dart` dispose**: Replace lazy `.map()` (which creates an iterable but never iterates it) with eager `for` loops to actually cancel subscriptions
- **`chat.dart`**: Cancel `_timestampTimer` in `dispose()`, add `mounted` guard in `_handleHideStickyTimestamp()`
- **`get_preview_url_mixin.dart`**: Store stream subscription, expose `disposeGetPreviewUrlMixin()` to cancel it
- **`twake_link_preview.dart`** and **`chat_details_links_item.dart`**: Call `disposeGetPreviewUrlMixin()` in `dispose()`

### Stream filtering
- **`chat.dart`**: Filter `onEvent.stream` with `.where(roomID == room?.id)` — events from other rooms are discarded before reaching the listener
- **`connection_status_header.dart`**: Use `.map((s) => s.status).distinct()` instead of rebuilding on every sync progress update
- **`matrix.dart`**: Add `.where((sync) => sync.presence?.isNotEmpty ?? false)` to skip syncs with no presence data

## Why
- The `.map((s) => s.cancel())` in `dispose()` was a **silent bug** — `.map()` returns a lazy iterable that was never consumed, so subscriptions were never actually cancelled
- Unfiltered event streams caused listener callbacks for events that were immediately discarded (wrong room, no presence data, same sync status)
